paper.title_en: Transformer Partial Discharge Detection Using Continuous-Wave Fixed-Frequency NV-Center Quantum Sensing
paper.abstract_en: Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center quantum sensing provides electrical insulation, electromagnetic-interference immunity, and fast transient-response capability, making it a promising technique for noncontact partial discharge (PD) detection in power transformers. However, conventional frequency-swept optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) methods are unsuitable for resolving nanosecond-scale transient magnetic fields generated by PD pulses. To address this limitation, this article proposes a noncontact transformer PD detection method based on continuous-wave fixed-frequency detection using diamond NV centers. A coupling model among PD pulse current, transient magnetic field around the grounding lead, and fluorescence response is established, clarifying the dependence of detection sensitivity on the operating-point slope and system noise. The laser and microwave (MW) powers are jointly optimized, and an all-fiber sensing probe integrated with a compact MW antenna is developed. Finite-element simulation indicates that the probe should be positioned 2.5 cm from the grounding lead with the NV-axis tangential to the local circumferential magnetic field. Synchronous high-voltage experiments show that, at an apparent charge of 13.4 pC, the proposed system achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of 5.78 dB and an apparent-charge response coefficient approximately 99.3 times that of a high-frequency current transformer (HFCT). The average peak-to-peak output exhibits strong linearity with apparent charge, with a coefficient of determination of 0.995 and a theoretical minimum detectable apparent charge of 9.1 pC. The proposed compensation strategy effectively suppresses temperature-induced baseline drift, supporting stable long-term operation in complex electromagnetic environments.
